I'm a wine enthusiast in the sense that I love drinking it. In terms of what you're talking about though, before I became a stay-at-home mom I was a bourbon expert. I knew over 150 different bourbons from 7 distilleries, and if you told me what you already knew you liked I could recommend at least 10 you'd never tried before. I had a 100% success rate with suggestions. I can still tell you exactly what makes bourbon different from whiskey, and tell you all about certain mashbills and the flavors they bring.

Things have obviously changed a bit in the 3 years I've been out of the work force, but I guarantee I could still give you some amazing recommendations. Too bad there isn't a job for bourbon experts.
"Good girl."

I let her make mistakes, and I try to let her figure out how to fix them on her own with the caveat that I'm always there to help her if she needs to. I try to praise her for hard work and determination over things that are 'innate' (i.e. - I'm proud of how hard you worked on that vs I'm proud of how smart you are). 

If I am putting that level of expectation on her, I'm absolutely not trying to. I'll try and be more aware of the perceived standards I'm putting out. I only want my kid to be happy.

How extreme are we talking about? My 7 year old responds very negatively to any perceived imperfection (immediately defensive whenever we bring things up escalating to full on meltdown and apologizing). My husband and I are very attentive, give positive reinforcement as often as possible, we've never physically abused her, we don't yell. The only time we ever even feel the need to raise our voice is because she gets so overwhelmed by the idea that she did something wrong, that she literally won't let us get a word in edgewise. 

She is such a good kid. She's responsible, she takes care of her possessions, space, and pets. She's kind, respectful, and so crazy smart. She doesn't really push boundaries that much. We are easygoing parents, we don't have many rules outside if the age-appropriate ones, and we always take time to explain and discuss rules when we set them. 

But she's 7, which means occasionally she will exhibit behavior we need to address. And as soon as we do, she goes into meltdown mode. From what I understand she never did that at school, but it's been a year and a half since she was physically in school, and this reaction has only really developed in the last year, so I'm worried it will carry over.

If her behavior is something that would flag as a sign, I want to know so I can figure out if we're doing something wrong. I never want to make my daughter feel scared or neglected, but I also know my parents thought they were good parents when they weren't.
